page.layout: One page of running text in a single full-width column. No margin notes, no footnotes. Printed page number "30" and running head "CANTICUM MOSIS" at the top. A catchword "ter-" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: quod jure poterat partim divino, ut filius Dei & hæres omnium, partim acquisito per redemptionem populi in peculium suum. Imo & justus dicitur, dum sine omni prosopolepsiâ ad se confugientes suscipit, atque pro jure donato gratiose excipit; alias vero ut hostes arcet & oppugnat: à quo titulo Messias sæpius commendatur ut justus, suo jure utens. Jes. 11: 2. 53: 11. Jer. 23: 5. 6. 33; 15. 16. Zach. 9: 9.

Rectus quoque dicitur propter intrinsecam sanctitatem (quæ est purus amor & studium recti) utpote nullâ pravitate notatus: sicuti erat homo, quem Deus condiderat, antequam ratiocinia quæsiverat יָשָׁר rectus. Eccl. 7: 29. & Deus ipse dicitur יָשָׁר Psal. 25: 8. Hæc etiam opponuntur criminibus objectis, quasi fraude doloque egerit, & non ex jure suo, aut non ex rectâ intentione.

Vers. 5. Hic versus magnam interpretibus peperit difficultatem, qui circa ejus sensum mirum in modum variant: ut verè obtineat hic, quot capita, tot sensus; oriturque varietas ob dubium subjecti, ad quod verba שחת לו[?] sint referenda. Plurimi interpretes tanquam caput accusationis populi corrupti accipiunt, atque ut crimen progenici perversæ exponunt. Hinc Junius vertit corrupit se nempe Israël. Vulgatus peccavit ei, alii corrupit sibi. LXX peccarunt non ei. Hæc interpretantur viri Docti, nihil suo scelere Deo officere potuerunt; sed se ipsos potuis (ut vertunt Symmachus, Aquila & Pagninus) corruperunt, atque illustrant ex loco Iob. 35: 6. Verum ἀβλεψία[?] interpretum in causa est, quod in veram dictorum mentem non incidentes, in has difficultates prolapsi fuerint. Quod si locum ipsum juxta accentuationem Hebraicam attentius inspexissent, non ut puto adeo contorta produxissent in-

page.notes: Printed text is set in roman with some italic Latin quotations and names; the exact extent of italics in the third paragraph is uncertain. "ἀβλεψία" is read from a small Greek word at the scan's resolution and is uncertain. The Hebrew pointing in "יָשָׁר" (both occurrences) and "שחת לו" is read from a low-resolution scan; the final letters of "שחת לו" are doubtful. "potuis" is printed as such and is probably a printing error for "potius"; left as printed. The figure after "23:" in the Jer. reference looks like an old-style 5 and is transcribed as 5. The "ter-" line at the foot is treated as the catchword, since the text ends with "in-" on the line above it. A small star-like mark under the text is a printer's mark and is omitted.
